turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning uncle, I'm Dr Lim from anaesthesia. I just want to go through a few things before your hip operation. Is it okay if your daughter helps answer some questions too?

turns.speaker: CAREGIVER
turns.text: Yes doctor, I'm his daughter, I can help translate if needed.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you. Can you tell me what happened, how did the fall happen?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I slipped in the bathroom yesterday evening lah, my hip very pain, cannot stand up after that.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Now, your chart says you're on apixaban for your heart rhythm — that's a blood thinner. This is important: when exactly was the last time you took it? Can you confirm the date and roughly what time?

turns.speaker: CAREGIVER
turns.text: Actually doctor, I need to correct the nursing note — it says three days ago but that's not right.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Aiyah, I got confused which day it was lah, everything mixed up after the fall.

turns.speaker: CAREGIVER
turns.text: He actually took his apixaban yesterday morning, so that's only about fourteen hours before surgery, not three days ago like it says in the records. I saw him take it myself before we came to the hospital.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for catching that, that changes our plan — we may need to avoid spinal injection this close to the last dose, or manage it very carefully. Any allergies I should know about?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Penicillin, I get rash last time in hospital.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Noted, no penicillin. Any other medications — for your heart, or your kidneys?

turns.speaker: CAREGIVER
turns.text: Bisoprolol for his heart rate, atorvastatin for cholesterol. He used to take furosemide for fluid but the polyclinic stopped that about six months ago.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. And when did you last eat or drink?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Nothing since last night's dinner, maybe seven something.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good, that's within our fasting window. Have you had anaesthesia before?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, for my other knee in 2019, spinal jab only, no problem that time.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good to know. We'll aim for a similar spinal approach today if the timing allows, with sedation, and I'll explain the back-up plan in case we need to convert to a full general anaesthetic.
